claims.claim_ar: جملة (أَنْ + فعل) تكون مَفْعُولاً لَهُ (مفعول له) مع أفعال المعنى كـ الطمع
claims.claim_en: An 'an' clause (أن + verb) functions as a maph'ool lahu (object / verbal complement) with verbs of expectation/hope such as طَمَعَ.

claims.claim_ar: يَجُوزُ أن يكونَ فَرِيقٌ مبتدأً أو خبرًا (أي: أن يكون مبتدأً وخبرًا في تركيبٍ شبيه)
claims.claim_en: It is permissible for 'فَرِيقٌ' to be analyzed as a mubtada' or as a khabar (i.e., it can function as subject/predicate in such constructions).
claims.needs_review_reason: The source speaks generally about the pattern (مِنْهُمْ مَنْ ...) — mapping this permissibility onto this specific verse (where كان + فريق) is plausible but should be cross-checked with the verse-level syntactic context.

claims.source_quote_ar: يَجُوزُ أَنْ يكون مِنْهُم رَافعا لمن
claims.claim_ar: يجوز أن يكونَ (مِنْهُمْ) رافعًا (أي: أن تؤخذ في محل رفع في بعض وجوه الإعراب لهذا التركيب)
claims.claim_en: It is permissible to treat 'مِنْهُمْ' as raised (nominative/subject-like) in some analyses of this construction.
claims.needs_review_reason: Treating the prepositional phrase مِنهُم as 'رافِع' is an atypical reading (since مِنْ is normally genitive); the source states it as a permissible reading for constructions like 'مِنْهُمْ مَنْ ...' and needs checking against this verse's morphology and prosody.

claims.claim_ar: قد تُؤوّلُ الجملةُ نَعْتًا لِـ(رُسُلٍ) في مثل هذا التركيب (الجملة نعتٌ لِرُسُلٍ)
claims.claim_en: The clause may be an adjective/appositive (نعت) to 'messengers' in constructions of this type.
claims.needs_review_reason: The source example explicitly mentions رُسُلٍ; that referent does not occur in S2:75, so applying this exact appositive relation to the present verse is speculative and requires review.

claims.claim_ar: يجوز أن تكونَ هذه الجملةُ مستأنفةً (أي: أنها جملةٌ مُستأنَفَة وليسُ تابعةً بالضرورة)
claims.claim_en: The clause may be taken as a resumed/resumptive clause (مستأنف) in some analyses of the pattern.
claims.needs_review_reason: The source gives this as an alternate structural possibility for the cited pattern; whether the clause in S2:75 is best read as مستأنف requires checking the wider discourse connection.

warnings: The cited source discusses the pattern in the example '(مِنْهُمْ مَنْ قَصَصْنَا)'. The extracted claims are taken from those general remarks and applied to Sura 2:75; verify that the example's referents and context align with the syntactic relations in S2:75.

The source's explicit example for the 'مَفْعُولٌ لَهُ' reading uses the negative example 'أَنْ لَا يَكُونُوا' while the verse has 'أَنْ يُؤْمِنُوا'. The general rule (أن‑clause as مفعولٌ لَهُ) applies, but confirm semantic/verb-class matching when mapping to this verse.
